Training-free approach that requires no model retraining, enabling practical adoption to existing diffusion LLMs

Well-motivated problem identification addressing two concrete bottlenecks (lack of KV cache support and parallel decoding quality degradation) preventing diffusion LLMs from being practical alternatives to autoregressive models
Novel block-wise KV cache design cleverly adapted for bidirectional attention in diffusion models, with convincing empirical support from KV activation similarity analysis (Figure 3)

Solid theoretical contribution with Theorem 1 providing formal characterization of when parallel decoding with independent marginals is equivalent to sequential decoding, including bounds on approximation error
Comprehensive experimental validation including extensive ablations on prefill length, generation length, cache block size, confidence thresholds, and clear component-wise contribution analysis
Clear presentation with effective visualizations, well-organized tables, logical progression, and explicit algorithm description (Algorithm 1)
weaknesses: Moderate novelty in KV cache component—KV caching is well-established; the adaptation to diffusion models is relatively straightforward (reuse within blocks, recompute after). strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real efficiency gap in diffusion LLMs lacking KV cache support and suffering from parallel decoding quality degradation
Strong empirical results: achieves up to 27.6× speedup with minimal accuracy loss (±1-2 points) across multiple models and benchmarks

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: systematic testing on LLaDA, Dream, LLaDA-V across GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, MathVista, MathVerse with detailed ablations on block size, thresholds, and prefill/generation lengths
Solid theoretical contribution: Theorem 1 formally justifies parallel decoding with high-confidence tokens, including tight equivalence bounds and comprehensive divergence analysis (KL, L_p, TV)
Training-free approach: practical advantage enabling immediate deployment without model retraining
Excellent presentation: clear writing, convincing visualizations (Figure 3 heatmaps), thorough proofs, and extensive appendices demonstrating rigor
Generalizes across model architectures and task types: speedups consistent across different models (LLaDA/Dream variants) and problem domains (math, code, vision-language)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: block-wise KV cache and confidence-thresholding are incremental adaptations of straightforward ideas rather than significant algorithmic advances

Theory-practice gap in Theorem 1: assumes well-defined joint p_θ violating MDM properties (acknowledged but implications unclear); tight bound ε≤1/(n+1) and connection to practical threshold τ=0.9 not rigorously justified

KV cache approximation lacks rigor: no formal error quantification despite 'negligible performance drop' claims; multimodal LLaDA-V requires completely different strategy (full blocks + refresh) due to >8% accuracy degradation with small blocks, indicating fundamental limitations

Batch size scalability limitations (Section C.5): both PrefixCache and LLaDA plateau after batch size 8 while autoregressive LLaMA scales smoothly, severely limiting high-throughput deployment applicability

Hyperparameter brittleness: cache block size (Figure 4), confidence threshold, and factor require tuning with high sensitivity; different strategies needed for different models; limited principled guidance for practitioners on hyperparameter selection

Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing comparisons to Block Diffusion [1] and other diffusion acceleration techniques; no comparison to speculative decoding or generic inference acceleration methods
Limited model coverage: only tested on masked diffusion models (LLaDA, Dream); no evaluation on SEDD, CTMC, or other discrete diffusion approaches; generalization unclear
Statistical rigor: no confidence intervals or significance tests; some accuracy changes (1-2 points) within potential noise margins; missing multi-run analysis
Confidence metric unexplored: uses max softmax without ablation; no investigation of alternative confidence functions or their impact on theoretical guarantees
Algorithm and evaluation details: unclear specification in Algorithm 1 (line 6); missing latency percentiles and memory consumption analysis; some results relegated to appendix

strengths: Strong empirical speedup results (8-27×) across multiple models (LLaDA, Dream, LLaDA-V) and tasks (GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP)
Training-free approach with immediate practical applicability to existing diffusion LLMs
Well-motivated technical design justified by cosine similarity analysis (Figure 3) of KV activations
Comprehensive ablation studies examining cache block size, prefill/generation lengths, and strategy variants
Extensive experiments including multimodal evaluation and varying sequence lengths
Theoretical analysis (Theorem 1) providing formal justification for confidence-aware decoding with divergence bounds
weaknesses: Limited novelty: block-wise caching for diffusion models (Block Diffusion [1]) and confidence-based token selection are not new; paper combines existing techniques without deep integration

Theoretical limitations: Theorem 1 relies on 'well-defined joint PMF' assumption that authors acknowledge MDMs may not satisfy (Remark 1); bounds are worst-case and empirical validation of conditions never provided; tight bounds (n+1)ε≤1 impractical for n>3

Technical soundness concerns: insufficient justification for KV cache approximation validity in bidirectional full-attention models; only demonstrates similarity within blocks, not across blocks; no error accumulation analysis

Incomplete experimental comparisons: no baseline against other acceleration methods (distillation, quantization, speculative decoding); claims to 'close gap with AR models' contradicted by Figure 1(a) and Section C.5 showing poor scaling with batch size; LLaMA continues outperforming at large batch sizes
Accuracy degradation inconsistency: claims 'minimal' loss but Table 2 shows 2-3% drops in some cases; no principled threshold for acceptable degradation

strengths: Addresses practical efficiency problem in emerging diffusion LLM models with training-free approach
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (LLaDA, Dream, LLaDA-V) and diverse benchmarks with extensive ablation studies
Well-motivated technical approach with empirical observation of high KV activation similarity (Figure 3) and clear identification of parallel decoding degradation root cause
Impressive speedup results (up to 27.6×) with minimal accuracy loss (1-2 points), demonstrated across text and multimodal tasks
Theorem 1 provides formal theoretical justification for confidence-based parallel decoding with explicit divergence bounds
Clear presentation with informative visualizations and detailed appendix including qualitative analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: KV caching is well-established; confidence-based selection is incremental over LLaDA's top-K approach
